title: SRE oncall sentinel runbook - quick draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact on-call-focused runbook (quick draft) for the most recurring API failure modes we see: 5xx/timeouts, 429s (rate limiting), degraded streaming (partial responses/stalls), and sudden elevated error rates.

Scope and intent:
- Not a formal postmortem; a slim, actionable checklist for responders who need to get services back to SLO quickly.
- Emphasize safety: preserve customer traffic, reduce blast radius, restore streaming where possible, and collect evidence for followup.
- Includes short mitigation recipes + key queries/commands.

Signals that trigger this runbook (examples):
- Alert: API_latency_p50 > 400ms and p95 > 2s for 5m
- Alert: API_5xx_rate > 1% and rising
- Alert: Edge_streaming_error_rate > 0.5% with increased client disconnects
- Alert: RateLimit_429s spike correlated with increased traffic from specific routes
- Pager: user-visible error reports / customer slack thread

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge pager, announce on #sre-ops with short status line and ETA: "oncall: investigating, ETA 15m"
2) Determine scope: Use dashboards - filter by region, model, route.
   - Is it global, region, or a single model/route?
   - Are internal pings/health checks failing?
3) Capture evidence: timestamps, example request ids (x-request-id), stack traces, gateway logs.
4) If errors/latency affect critical customers, enable mitigation flags (see mitigation section).
5) Assign a second responder to communications/customer messages.

Common root buckets to check in parallel:
- Upstream infrastructure (GPUs overloaded, autoscaler stuck)
- Networking (NLB/ALB errors, connection churn, TLS handshake failures)
- Backend service regression (new rollout, config change, model change)
- Thundering herd / traffic spike causing backpressure (queue growth, memory spikes)
- Degraded dependency (auth, billing, KMS)

Commands & queries (examples you can paste):
- Get recent failed requests (gateway logs):
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="http_load_balancer" AND severity>=ERROR AND jsonPayload.requestPath: "/v1/*"' --limit 50 --order=timestamp
- Prometheus example (latency):
  sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"0.5\"}[5m])) by (route)
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route))
- Find top 10 routes returning 429s:
  topk(10, sum(rate(api_responses_total{code=~"429"}[5m])) by (route))
- Check streaming error rate and active streams:
  rate(api_stream_errors_total[1m])
  api_active_streams{state="open"}
- Quick health of serving hosts (k8s cluster):
  kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | egrep "CrashLoop|Error|NotReady"
  kubectl -n inference logs <pod> --since=10m | tail -n 200

Mitigations by failure mode (short recipes):
A) Timeouts / elevated latency: (fastest wins)
- If p95 latency is breaching SLO and CPU/GPU utilization is high:
  - Immediately reduce concurrency: flip route-level concurrency cap to 50% for suspect routes (console or config flag).
  - If autoscaler is not scaling: toggle manual scale up of GPU pool for Dedicated or restart the horizontal autoscaler controller (investigate by HPA status).
  - Enable degraded mode: return cached responses for safe routes (where cacheable).
  - Route degradations: temporarily route traffic to a lower-latency model variant (quantized or smaller) with automatic notice to customers.
- Preserve logs and set retention snapshot for affected nodes.

B) 429s (rate limiting spikes):
- Quick check: are 429s caused by the platform egress (we throttled) or a downstream quota?
  - Look at rate_limit_decision logs and per-account quotas.
- If platform-side: increase limits for the affected route/group temporarily or switch to burst pool (console > routing > burst).
- If client misbehaving (one customer floods): apply tenant-level backoff or cut them to a lower tier; contact Customer Success for high-value customers before cutting.
- As an emergency: enable conservative global cache of frequent prompts to reduce request rate.

C) Degraded streaming (partial responses, stalls):
- First determine failure mode: server stalls vs network drops vs client timeouts.
- Check connection churn on LBs: 502/504 patterns, keepalive logs. If LB is dropping connections, restart the target group.
- If backend KV cache miss storm causing repeated full model evals: enable prefix cache or reduce beam size, temporarily disable long-context experiments.
- If one model instance type is affected, cordon node and redirect traffic to healthy nodes.
- For consumer-facing streaming: provide fallback to non-streamed responses with a header X-Fallback-Streaming: true.

D) Elevated 5xx/error rates:
- Pinpoint: correlate errors to release/tag: look at request headers (x-deployed-version).
- If correlated to a recent rollout: initiate fast rollback to previous stable version (console rollback button or k8s rollout undo).
- If caused by dependency failures: toggle degraded mode to return 503 with Retry-After for non-critical routes, preserve capacity for priority customers.
- Open immediate incident ticket and capture stack traces, heap profiles if memory anomalies suspected.

Escalation matrix and communication: (short)
- If mitigations restore service within 30m: continue monitoring, prepare incident timeline, handoff to post-incident owner.
- If not restored in 30m or customer-impact > 10%: escalate to SRE lead (Ethan Brooks) and on-call infra (+product SMEs).
- Notify CS for impacted accounts and provide regular 15m updates. Use incident template in #incident-ops.

Quick templates (copy-paste)
Slack initial: "oncall: investigating elevated API errors (timeouts/5xx/429) affecting routes X,Y. ETA 15m. Working on mitigations: reducing concurrency + routing to fallbacks. Will update every 15m. x-request-ids: <id1>,<id2>"
Customer note short: "We are investigating higher-than-normal errors on our API calls. Our SREs are actively mitigating. We will provide an update in 15 minutes and follow up with root cause and mitigation details."

Post-incident actions (when incident stabilized):
- Create incident postmortem draft within 48h. Include timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations taken, and follow-up owners.
- Schedule a 1-hour RCA with eng/product/devex if rollout/config change suspected.
- Mandatory follow-ups: ensure alert thresholds and dashboards are adjusted to reduce noise; add a synthetic test for the failing route.
- If autoscaler or scale settings were toggled, define a safe automation guard to prevent repeated toggles without human approval.

Known TODOs / experiments to add to this doc:
- Add a short script to toggle per-route concurrency via CLI (with safe guards).
- Flesh out tenant-level backoff policy and standardized customer communications.
- Add more precise PromQL examples for our current metrics naming schema.
- Add runbook snippets for specific customer-impacting product flows (embeddings vs chat vs rerank).

Notes to self / scratch: (messy)
- We often forget to snapshot heap profiles before restart — enforce automatic profiler dump when p95 mem > threshold.
- Check interplay between prefix cache TTL and model version pinning — cache invalidation can trigger big load.
- Consider a "streaming-limited" flag at LB edge to turn streaming into polled responses for a tenant.

References and evidence links:
- Dashboard: api-prod/latency-and-errors (internal link)
- Confluence draft: /display/SRE/streaming-fallback-design (TODO: write detailed design)
- Incident SRE-412 (example) - link above

End of quick draft. This file is intentionally terse and operator-focused. Share feedback in the doc or ping on #sre-ops.
